title: Strawberry & Rhubarb Streusel Muffins
changes_from_base: Diced rhubarb macerated in sugar and fresh strawberries replace the blueberries; a brown sugar streusel goes on top instead of lemon sugar.
summary: Tender muffins packed with sugared rhubarb and fresh strawberries, finished with brown sugar streusel.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Macerate
steps.text: Stir the diced rhubarb with the caster sugar in a small bowl and leave it for 20 min so the sugar draws out some pink juice. Meanwhile heat the oven to 190 °C (170 °C fan) and line the tin with cases.

steps.title: Streusel
steps.text: Rub the 60 g flour, the streusel brown sugar and the cold butter between your fingertips until you have pea-sized clumps. Keep it in the fridge until needed.

steps.title: Dry
steps.text: In a large bowl, whisk the 280 g flour with the muffin brown sugar, baking powder and salt, breaking up any lumps of sugar.

steps.title: Wet
steps.text: Whisk the milk, eggs, cooled melted butter and vanilla in a jug, pour into the flour and stir with a spatula until barely mixed; a few lumps are fine.

steps.title: Fruit
steps.text: Fold in the rhubarb with all its syrup and the diced strawberries in a few turns, stopping as soon as the fruit is spread through.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Fill the cases about three-quarters full, pile the cold streusel on top and bake 22-25 min, until the crumb is golden and a cocktail stick comes out clean of raw batter.

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: Leave in the tin 10 min so the fruit settles, then lift onto the rack.

tips: The most common mistake is stirring the batter smooth; overmixing with all that wet fruit gives tough, tunnelled muffins.
Frozen rhubarb works; thaw it and drain off the water before macerating.
Keep the streusel cold so it stays in crunchy lumps in the oven.
storage: Best on the day. Keep in an airtight box at room temperature for up to 2 days, or freeze for up to 1 month. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
